leftEvidence.role: The cross in letters and later memory
leftEvidence.title: Righteousness manifested; redemption in Christ Jesus

points.label: Action and sequence
points.left: Paul speaks of righteousness apart from law yet witnessed by law and prophets, redemption in Christ Jesus, his blood, and God’s justice.
points.right: Weak, ungodly, sinners, and enemies describe the people for whom Christ dies.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.
points.right: The passage compares a rare human death with Christ’s death while refusing to describe its recipients as deserving.

payload.posture: Romans develops the significance of Christ’s death through distinct arguments about righteousness and reconciliation.

rightEvidence.role: The cross in letters and later memory
rightEvidence.title: Christ dies for the ungodly while they are enemies

payload.tension: The first passage centers manifested righteousness, redemption, blood, and God’s justice; the second centers weakness, enemies, death, blood, rescue, and rejoicing.
payload.title: Redemption displayed / enemies reconciled
